hypothesis: The qwen36 CUDA chain stages a prompt chunk's non-resident experts from the tier's host pool (page-locked RAM), which holds the experts off the card at the warm start. The chain's promotions and the tier's swaps move experts off the card later; #2416's follow page-locks them only before a chunk of 128 rows or more, and a smaller chunk's layer holding one goes to the host's step. Page-locking the residents' RAM copies too, when the card holds fewer than every expert (a Colab T4 holds 6605 of the 10240), keeps every such layer on the card, so a short prompt after an answer is faster.
command: bench.c built against c/ (make CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as bench build does); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 64,512,64 --gen 32 --teacher

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads, 38.5 MiB L3) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.storage: Google Colab VM disk (the model downloaded to /content before the runs)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), driver 580.82.07, gcc 13.3.0

config.scenario: the third length of the base: a 64-token prompt after a 64-token and a 512-token prompt, each with its 32 decode steps, in one process
config.tok_s: prompt tokens / the prompt's seconds (bench's prefill_tps of the third row)
config.engine_build: the stack of our open PRs: origin/dev c1c06ac6 + #2015, #2016, #2413, #2414, #2415, #2416, #2417, #2418, #2421, #2422, #2423, #2424, #2425 and #2428 at their heads, records-only commits left out (79fe45ac, local)

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64) on this change; make -C c cuda-test on the T4 on it (correctness.txt). Where nothing moved the logits are the same: the stack and the stack + this change at 64, 128 and 256 tokens. After experts left the card a chunk's layer that went to the host's step runs on the card: the stack + this change gives the fingerprint, nll and top1 of the stack with #2416's follow before every staged chunk, in every row of the base (logits.txt). The 64-token prompt after the 512 here: v0 ['ad3b695857d1fcca'], v1 ['162b220baca4184c'].
